title: Client Connector-based end user notifications from the ZIA side: prerequisites, channels, details, shared settings and languages

prereqs-inline-web-and-cac.statement: For Inline Web DLP and Cloud App Control EUNs, Client Connector needs Endpoint DLP (which includes EUN) or EUN as a standalone feature, which requires Windows 4.6.0.123 or later or macOS 4.3.1.56 or later; in Internet & SaaS, Zscaler Support is contacted to enable EUN for each of the two policies.

evidence.after: Before configuring Zscaler Client Connector EUNs, ensure that you meet the necessary requirements based on the policy type:
quotes: | In Zscaler Client Connector | Endpoint DLP (includes EUN) or EUN as a standalone feature must be enabled. Standalone EUN feature requires: For Windows: 4.6.0.123 or later For macOS: 4.3.1.56 or later |
| In Internet & SaaS | Contact Zscaler Support to enable EUN for Inline Web DLP. |

evidence.after: | In Internet & SaaS | Endpoint DLP policy must be enabled. |
quotes: | In Zscaler Client Connector | Endpoint DLP (includes EUN) or EUN as a standalone feature must be enabled. Standalone EUN feature requires: For Windows: 4.6.0.123 or later For macOS: 4.3.1.56 or later |
| In Internet & SaaS | Contact Zscaler Support to enable EUN for Cloud App Control. |

prereqs-endpoint-dlp.statement: Endpoint DLP EUNs need Endpoint DLP enabled in Client Connector and the Endpoint DLP policy enabled in Internet & SaaS.

quotes: | In Zscaler Client Connector | Endpoint DLP must be enabled. |
| In Internet & SaaS | Endpoint DLP policy must be enabled. |

prereqs-firewall-dns-ips.statement: Firewall Filtering, DNS Control and IPS Control EUNs are supported on Windows devices running Client Connector 4.8 or later over Z-Tunnel 2.0. In Internet & SaaS they need Firewall Filtering enabled with Advanced Firewall, DNS Control enabled with Advanced DNS (provided by the Advanced Firewall), and IPS Control enabled through Advanced Firewall.

evidence.after: | In Internet & SaaS | Contact Zscaler Support to enable EUN for Cloud App Control. |
quotes: | In Zscaler Client Connector | Supported on Windows devices running Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 or later over Z-Tunnel 2.0. |
| In Internet & SaaS | Firewall Filtering policy must be enabled with Advanced Firewall. |

evidence.after: | In Internet & SaaS | Firewall Filtering policy must be enabled with Advanced Firewall. |
quotes: | In Zscaler Client Connector | Supported on Windows devices running Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 or later over Z-Tunnel 2.0. |
| In Internet & SaaS | DNS Control Policy must be enabled with Advanced DNS, which is provided by the Advanced Firewall. |

evidence.after: | In Internet & SaaS | DNS Control Policy must be enabled with Advanced DNS, which is provided by the Advanced Firewall. |
quotes: | In Zscaler Client Connector | Supported on Windows devices running Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 or later over Z-Tunnel 2.0. |
| In Internet & SaaS | IPS Control policy must be enabled through Advanced Firewall. |

app-profile-web.statement: For Inline Web DLP and Cloud App Control EUNs the app profile (Windows or macOS) must have Install Endpoint ZDP enabled; these EUNs are supported as a standalone feature without Endpoint DLP, the Endpoint ZDP agent activating Endpoint DLP (which includes EUN) or standalone EUN depending on the organization's subscription. Endpoint DLP EUNs need Endpoint DLP in Client Connector, and the same app profile step with Install Endpoint ZDP.

evidence.after: Ensure that you have EUN customization enabled for your organization and complete the necessary configurations depending on the policy type:
quotes: Configure an App Profile for your devices (Windows or macOS) and enable the Install Endpoint ZDP option.

EUNs for Inline Web DLP and Cloud App Control are supported as a standalone feature, without requiring Endpoint DLP. Depending on your organization's subscription, the Endpoint ZDP agent activates either Endpoint DLP (includes EUN) or standalone EUN.
You must have Endpoint DLP in Zscaler Client Connector to use these EUNs.

evidence.after: You must have Endpoint DLP in Zscaler Client Connector to use these EUNs.
quotes: Configure an App Profile for your devices (Windows or macOS) and enable the Install Endpoint ZDP option.

app-profile-network.statement: For Firewall Filtering, DNS Control and IPS Control EUNs the app profile is for Windows only, with the Zscaler Notification Framework enabled and a Notification Template selected that has ZIA Firewall and Firewall Popup, DNS and DNS Popup, or IPS and IPS Popup notifications enabled respectively.

quotes: Configure an App Profile for your devices (Windows only) and enable the Zscaler Notification Framework option. Additionally, you must select a Notification Template for your App Profile that has ZIA Firewall and Firewall Popup Notifications options enabled.
Additionally, you must select a Notification Template for your App Profile that has DNS and DNS Popup Notifications options enabled.

Configure an App Profile for your devices (Windows only) and enable the Zscaler Notification Framework Framework option. Additionally, you must select a Notification Template for your App Profile that has IPS and IPS Popup Notifications options enabled.

evidence.after: Additionally, you must select a Notification Template for your App Profile that has ZIA Firewall and Firewall Popup Notifications options enabled.
quotes: Configure an App Profile for your devices (Windows only) and enable the Zscaler Notification Framework option.

rule-binding.statement: After customizing the notifications, the respective policy rules are configured to show EUNs when a specific rule action is triggered and to select the notification message to display.

quotes: After customizing the notifications, you can configure the respective policy rules to show EUNs when a specific rule action is triggered and select the notification message to display.

shared-settings.statement: Organization name, logo, support details and notification duration, among other general settings, are shared by all Client Connector-based notifications across policies, and changes to the General Details are mirrored in the User Confirmation notification settings.

quotes: In addition to customizing the notification message, you can modify general settings, such as organization name, logo, support details, notification duration, and more. These attributes are shared by all Zscaler Client Connector-based notifications across policies.

Any changes made within this section are mirrored in the User Confirmation notification settings as these configurations are shared by Zscaler Client Connector EUNs and User Confirmation notifications.

notification-actions.statement: Notification actions are Learn More (opens the Notifications tab in Client Connector; enabled by default and non-editable), Do Not Disturb (opens the More tab), Open Corporate Policy (opens the URL entered), Open Containing Folder (opens the folder where files that triggered the block rule are quarantined; applicable only for Endpoint DLP policies that quarantine the original file) and Request Exemption (opens the Data Protection tab; applicable only for Endpoint DLP rules with the Block action).

quotes: Learn More: Opens the Notifications tab in Zscaler Client Connector. This option is enabled by default and is non-editable.
Do Not Disturb: Opens the More tab in Zscaler Client Connector where the user can control the notification settings.
Open Corporate Policy: Opens the URL specified in the text field.
Open Containing Folder: Opens the folder where files that triggered the block rule are quarantined.
This field is applicable only for Endpoint DLP policies that quarantine the original file.
Request Exemption: Opens the Data Protection tab in Zscaler Client Connector where users can request to be exempted from the block rule enforcement.
This field is applicable only for Endpoint DLP rules with the Block action.

logo-and-duration.statement: The logo must be a PNG file with a size limit of 20x20 pixels. Under Duration, the notification is set to close automatically or manually by the user; with the Auto Close option a duration after which it closes is chosen from a drop-down menu.

quotes: The logo must be a PNG file with a size limit of 20x20 pixels.

Under Duration, specify whether the notification must be closed automatically or manually by the user. If you choose the Auto Close option, you need to specify the duration after which the notification must be closed using the drop-down menu.

support-url-variables.statement: The support URL can contain a query string using the variables $filename, $destination, $triggered_rule, $action, $url, $url_category, $app_activity, $app_category and $zcc_user; in the vendor's example a ticket URL with name=$zcc_user and url_accessed=$url is prepopulated with the user's name and the URL that triggered the policy.

quotes: The URL can contain a query string that uses one or more variables supported by Zscaler.
$filename - $destination - $triggered_rule - $action - $url - $url_category - $app_activity - $app_category - $zcc_user

For example, https://support.example.com/path/to/CreateTicket?name=$zcc_user&url_accessed=$url can take users to a web page for raising a ticket that's prepopulated with the user's name and the URL that triggered the policy.

message-syntax.statement: On the Inline Web DLP page, links are embedded in message content as __url[Link text | example.com] (with a double underscore at the beginning) and line breaks are introduced with //n; custom notification messages can be edited, but the Channel field cannot be modified.

quotes: You can embed links in the message content by using the following format: __url[Link text | example.com] (note the double underscore at the beginning).
You can also introduce line breaks in the message content by using the //n character.
You can edit custom notification messages, but the Channel field cannot be modified.

channel-inline-web.statement: Inline Web DLP messages use the Inline Web channel with an Allow message (the service allows and logs the activity) and a Block message, and are supported for DLP rules with and without content inspection. Additional details are File Name, Destination, Rule Name, URL Category, URL and DLP Engines.

quotes: Channel: Select Inline Web.
Allow: Customize the notification message that appears when an end user's activity triggers a DLP rule, but the service allows and logs the activity.
Block: Customize the notification message that appears when an end user's activity triggers a DLP rule and the service blocks the activity.

The end user notification (EUN) is supported for DLP rules with content inspection (i.e., use Zscaler DLP engines) and without content inspection (i.e., rely only on specific criteria to filter data).
File Name: Include the name of the file that triggered the rule.
Destination: Include the destination IP address or domain name that triggered the rule.
Rule Name: Include the name of the triggered rule.
URL Category: Include the URL category that triggered the rule.
URL: Include the URL that triggered the rule.
DLP Engines: Include the DLP engines that triggered the rule.

channel-cloud-application.statement: Cloud App Control messages use the Cloud Application channel with a preconfigured message for the Block action, and EUNs are supported only for Block rules where application access is allowed but certain interactions are blocked (for example viewing a social networking site is allowed but posting content is blocked). Additional details are Destination, Rule Name, App Activity, URL and App Category.

quotes: Channel: Select Cloud Application.
A preconfigured message appears for the Block policy action in the selected language.

The end user notifications (EUN) are supported only for Block rules under specific conditions where application access is allowed, but certain interactions with the application are blocked (for example, viewing a social networking site is allowed, but posting content is blocked).
Destination: Include the destination IP address or domain name that triggered the rule.
Rule Name: Include the name of the triggered rule.
App Activity: Include the user activity performed in the cloud application that triggered the rule.
URL: Include the URL that triggered the rule.
App Category: Include the cloud application's category that triggered the rule.

channels-endpoint-dlp.statement: Endpoint DLP has a default notification for each supported channel, including Printing, Removable Storage, Network Share and Personal Cloud Storage. Each of those four channel sections lists an Allow and a Block message, and Removable Storage also has Protect, shown when the service encrypts an affected file (recipients must use the Zscaler service to decrypt it). Rules with the Confirm action use an EUN message customized separately.

quotes: The Zscaler service provides a default notification for each supported Endpoint DLP channel including Printing, Removable Storage, Network Share, and Personal Cloud Storage.
Allow: Customize the notification message that appears when an end user's activity triggers an Endpoint DLP rule, but the service allows the traffic and logs the activity.
Block: Customize the notification message that appears when an end user's activity triggers an Endpoint DLP rule and the service blocks the activity.

Protect: Customize the notification message that appears when an end user's activity triggers a rule and the service encrypts an affected file. When a file is encrypted, users who receive the file must use the Zscaler service to decrypt the file.
For Endpoint DLP rules that are configured with the Confirm action, the Zscaler service provides an EUN message that is customized separately.
Allow: Customize the notification message that appears when an end user's activity triggers an Endpoint DLP rule, but the service allows the traffic and logs the activity.
Block: Customize the notification message that appears when an end user's activity triggers an Endpoint DLP rule and the service blocks the activity.
Allow: Customize the notification message that appears when an end user's activity triggers an Endpoint DLP rule, but the service allows the traffic and logs the activity.
Block: Customize the notification message that appears when an end user's activity triggers an Endpoint DLP rule and the service blocks the activity.
Allow: Customize the notification message that appears when an end user's activity triggers an Endpoint DLP rule, but the service allows the traffic and logs the activity.
Block: Customize the notification message that appears when an end user's activity triggers an Endpoint DLP rule and the service blocks the activity.

details-endpoint-dlp.statement: In the Removable Storage section of the Endpoint DLP page, messages can include File Name, Destination, Rule Name and DLP Engines as additional details.

quotes: File Name: Include the name of the file that triggered the rule.
Destination: Include the destination IP address or domain name that triggered the rule.
Rule Name: Include the name of the triggered rule.
DLP Engines: Include the DLP engines that triggered the rule.

channel-firewall.statement: Firewall Filtering messages use the Firewall channel and apply to all block actions of the policy, including Block/Drop, Block/ICMP and Block/Reset. The EUN is for non-web traffic and fires only on a policy match with non-HTTP/HTTPS traffic: traffic on standard web ports such as 80, 443 and 8080 identified as HTTP or HTTPS does not trigger it. Additional details are Network Service, Server Destination IP, Network Application, Application Service Group, Client Source IP, Server Destination Port and Server Destination Protocol.

quotes: Channel: Select Firewall.
The EUN applies to all block actions of the Firewall Filtering policy, including Block/Drop, Block/ICMP, and Block/Reset actions.
The Firewall Filtering policy EUN is designated specifically for non-web traffic and the EUN is triggered only when there is a policy match with non-web traffic (i.e., non-HTTP/HTTPS traffic).
Traffic mapped to standard web ports such as 80, 443, and 8080 and identified as HTTP or HTTPS do not trigger this EUN.
Network Service: The network service that was matched.
Server Destination IP: The destination server's IP address or domain that was matched.
Network Application: The network application that was matched.
Application Service Group: The network application service group that was matched.
Client Source IP: The client's source IP address that was matched.
Server Destination Port: The destination server's port that was matched.
Server Destination Protocol: The protocol defined in the network service criteria that was matched.

channel-dns.statement: DNS Control messages use the DNS channel and notify when a DNS Control block or a DNS redirect happens: the Block message applies to both Block and Block with Response Code actions, and Redirect Response covers a DNS redirect. Additional details are Request Category, Response Category, Resolved IP, DNS Tunnel, Requested Domain, Server IP, Protocol and Resolved IP-Based Country.

quotes: When network traffic from your users' devices is blocked by the DNS Control policy or a DNS redirect is performed, the Zscaler service can notify users of the policy action through Zscaler Client Connector installed on users' endpoints.
Channel: Select DNS.
The Block message applies to both Block and Block with Response Code actions of the DNS Control policy.
Redirect Response: Customize the notification message that appears when a DNS redirect is performed.
Request Category: The URL category of the DNS request.
Response Category: The URL category of the DNS response.
Resolved IP: The IP address to which the DNS request was resolved.
DNS Tunnel: DNS tunnels and network applications identified in the DNS traffic.
Requested Domain: The domain name for which DNS resolution was requested.
Server IP: The DNS server IP address.
Protocol: The protocol used by the DNS request.
Resolved IP-Based Country: The country where the destination server is located.

channel-ips.statement: IPS Control messages use the IPS channel and notify when traffic is allowed or blocked by the IPS Control policy. Allow covers potentially malicious activity that the configured IPS policy allows, and the Block message applies to both Block/Drop and Block/Reset actions. Additional details are Threat Name, Threat Category, Threat Severity, Threat Score, Network Service, Server Destination IP and Destination Country.

quotes: When network traffic from your user devices is allowed or blocked by the IPS Control policy, the Zscaler service can notify users of the policy action through Zscaler Client Connector installed on users' endpoints.
Channel: Select IPS.
Allow: Customize the notification message that appears when the service detects potentially malicious activity but allows the traffic based on the configured IPS policy.
The Block message applies to both Block/Drop and Block/Reset actions of the IPS Control policy.
Threat Name: The name of the threat detected in the traffic.
Threat Category: The category of the threat detected in the traffic.
Threat Severity: The severity of the threat detected.
Threat Score: The score assigned to the threat detected.
Network Service: The network service identified in the traffic and matched with the rule.
Server Destination IP: The destination server's IP address.
Destination Country: The country where the destination server is located.

languages.statement: Client Connector EUNs support English, Chinese (Traditional), French, German, Japanese and Spanish, chosen from the OS language setting, with English displayed by default if the OS language is not one of them. Only the default messages are translated to all the languages; modifying the message in one language does not change the same message in the others, and customized messages are not translated automatically.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector supports the following languages for end user notifications (EUNs): - English - Chinese (Traditional) - French - German - Japanese - Spanish
The EUN language is based on the OS language setting in your system.
If your system's OS language is different from the EUN supported languages, Zscaler Client Connector displays EUNs in English, by default.
Only the default messages are translated to all the languages that the Zscaler Client Connector supports.
Modifying the message in a specific language does not impact the respective message in other languages. Zscaler Client Connector does not automatically translate customized messages.

auto-close-values.title: Auto Close duration values
auto-close-values.detail: The settings page says a duration is chosen from a drop-down menu when Auto Close is selected, but does not list the values.

other-platforms.title: Client Connector EUN support on platforms other than Windows and macOS
other-platforms.detail: The prerequisite tables name Windows and macOS (Windows only for Firewall Filtering, DNS Control and IPS Control). Linux, iOS and Android are not mentioned; this is an absence in the captured pages, not a statement that they are unsupported.
